deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics by Riemann. It is a printed page from a German antiquarian bookseller's catalogue: page 16, section 'Astronomie', with the imprint 'Druck von C. Schünemann' (a Bremen printer) at the foot. The previous folio is page 45 of the same kind of catalogue (natural history, gardening, and the start of 'Astronomie').

The page lists second-hand books with format, place, year (abbreviated, e.g. 832 = 1832), binding (br. = broschiert, Ppbd. = Pappband, Ldrbd. = Lederband, Hlbldrbd. = Halblederband, Hlbfzbd. = Halbfranzband, Pgmtbd. = Pergamentband), original price in Thaler in parentheses, and sale price in Thaler and Silbergroschen. Authors listed include Arago, Beer & Mädler, Bessel, Biot, Blaeu, Brandes, Burja, Diesterweg, Encke, Ferguson, de la Hire, Jahn, Ideler, Kästner, Lalande, Lindenau, Lomonosov, Mädler, Nürnberger, M. Ohm, Poselger, Rüdiger, Schröter and F. T. Schubert.

There is no derivation, formula or marginal annotation in Riemann's hand on this side. The sheet was evidently reused as scrap paper. The facing or next side (162r/163) carries Riemann's numerical work: products, logarithms such as 2,8041394, and ratios like 76,5714 = 1072/14 and 170,6667 = 3072/18. That work is not on this page.

Dating note: the catalogue includes Ohm, 'Die Dreieinigkeit der Kraft', Nürnberg 1860, and Zimmermann 1859 on the previous page. So the sheet was printed no earlier than 1860. Riemann's use of it must therefore postdate 1860, despite the bundle label 'MathNotizen1853'.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed bookseller's catalogue page (scrap paper) with no mathematical content by Riemann. Its only minor interest is archival: an imprint date of at least 1860 inside a bundle labelled 1853, which constrains the dating of the calculations on the reverse.
transcription_corrections: The currency sign after Thaler amounts is printed as a special Thaler symbol (rendered like ₰ in the previous-page transcription); the transcription silently normalizes it to 'Thlr.'. This is acceptable but should be noted.
Fladung entry: the image shows 'i0 Sgr.' with a damaged 1; read 10 Sgr. as transcribed.
Ferguson entry: the image reads 'J. Newton's principles', a printer's I/J for Isaac Newton; this is consistent with the transcription.
The page contains no handwritten annotations to add; the transcription faithfully reflects the printed text apart from minor abbreviation normalizations.
